common_name: Mrs. Cooksey Loquat (Large Yellow-Fleshed New Zealand Loquat)

planting.note: Plant a container-grown or grafted tree in spring in full sun in well-drained soil; Mrs. Cooksey is a New Zealand loquat selection valued for unusually large fruit and rich yellow flesh, and performs well as a dooryard tree in warm, sheltered Gulf Coast plantings.

directions: Plant in well-drained soil in full sun, siting the tree where late-winter bloom and the developing spring crop are sheltered from the coldest north winds, since freezing temperatures during flowering or early fruit set are the main threat to a reliable harvest along the Gulf Coast. Mrs. Cooksey is a long-cultivated New Zealand loquat variety prized for its large fruit, typically running up to about 1.5 inches long and 1 inch in diameter, notably bigger than many older loquat selections. The flesh is a rich yellow color with very good, well-balanced sweet-tart flavor, and the tree bears reliably once established. Like other loquats it flowers in fall to winter and ripens over a short window in late winter into spring, so a warm microclimate or wall planting helps protect the bloom in zone 8 gardens; established trees tolerate light freezes, but open flowers and small green fruit are damaged well above the hardiness threshold of the wood itself. Thin heavy fruit clusters after set to improve individual fruit size, and harvest when fruit has fully colored and softens slightly, since loquats do not continue to ripen after picking.
sources: California Rare Fruit Growers Association - Loquat Fruit Facts
